statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-47262 (GO-2026-5475, GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq): when containerd created a container from a crafted image, it read the image's user and group database without a size bound, so the containerd daemon could exhaust memory and be OOM-killed. It is fixed in containerd 2.3.2, 2.2.5, 2.1.9, 2.0.10 and 1.7.33 by bounding the /etc/passwd and /etc/group reads in openUserFile in containerd's pkg/oci package (https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5475, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.3.2, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.2.5). Read the Go build information and the function table (with a reader of the Go symbol table that also works on stripped binaries) of every Go program in every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 89 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only, every download checked against the index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. Each package holds one file, the frontend Go program /usr/bin/build. runtime.main is found in the function table of every Go program scanned, so the tables were read. The build information of the frontend program lists github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 v2.2.0 through v2.3.7 across the builds, but the vulnerable code is not linked in. In every build, the only containerd packages in its function table are core/remotes/docker, core/remotes/docker/auth, core/remotes/errors, internal/lazyregexp, pkg/identifiers, pkg/reference and version (all under github.com/containerd/containerd/v2), and no function table of any Go program in any build contains a function from containerd's pkg/oci package. As a positive control, the same reader lists pkg/oci functions, including github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/pkg/oci.openUserFile, in /usr/bin/containerd from the DHI containerd 2.4.2-r5 package. The vulnerable code is not present in this package, so the containerd version recorded in its build information does not make it affected.

CVE-2026-47262 (GO-2026-5475, GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq): when containerd creates a container from a crafted image, it reads the image's /etc/passwd and /etc/group without a size limit, so an oversized or unusual file exhausts memory and the containerd process is killed. It is fixed in containerd 1.7.33, 2.0.10, 2.1.9, 2.2.5 and 2.3.2. The Go vulnerability database lists no symbols. The fix bounds the user-database reads in containerd's OCI spec options: on release/2.3, commit ff1d116ef9c2d7505306d7d367ef46ff0756460b changes openUserFile in pkg/oci/spec_opts.go; on release/1.7, commit 9ab2b7a894d15738f8323f69def272c29277b57f changes WithAppendAdditionalGroups, UserFromPath, GIDFromPath and getSupplementalGroupsFromPath in oci/spec_opts.go. Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5475, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/ff1d116ef9c2d7505306d7d367ef46ff0756460b, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/9ab2b7a894d15738f8323f69def272c29277b57f . We checked every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the repository index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read its Go build information (go version -m) and its function table (go tool nm), and searched its raw bytes, which also finds the names of inlined functions. The Go build information lists github.com/containerd/containerd 1.7.29 to 1.7.32 in builds before 0.71.0-r0, and github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 2.2.0 to 2.2.4 before 0.71.0-r0 and 2.3.1 in 0.71.0-r0 and 0.71.0-r1, inside the affected ranges; from 0.71.2-r0 on the builds carry containerd/v2 2.3.2 to 2.3.7 and no 1.x module. trivy links containerd's client and image packages, but in every build the function table has no user or group function of containerd's OCI spec package (oci or pkg/oci): openUserFile, WithUser, WithUsername, WithAdditionalGIDs, WithAppendAdditionalGroups, UserFromPath, GIDFromPath, UserFromFS, GIDFromFS and getSupplementalGroupsFromPath are absent. Before 0.74.0-r8 no pkg/oci function has its own function-table entry; from 0.74.0-r8 on only its CPU helpers appendCPUThrottlePaths, possibleCPUs and parsePossibleCPUs and its package initializers do. The user-database parser it calls, github.com/moby/sys/user, is present only as its package initializer user.init, while runtime.main is. The raw-byte search of every build finds, under containerd's OCI package, only the inlined descriptor converters DescriptorFromProto and DescriptorToProto, the CPU helpers and initializers above, and the source paths of pkg/oci/spec.go and spec_linux.go; it finds no source path for spec_opts.go, where the user-database code lives, and no openUserFile, openBoundedUserFile, getSupplementalGroupsFromPath, user.ParseGroup or user.ParsePasswd string. As a positive control, the same function-table and byte searches on programs built against containerd 2.3.1 (calling oci.WithUser, WithAdditionalGIDs and WithAppendAdditionalGroups) and containerd 1.7.29 (calling oci.UserFromPath, GIDFromPath and WithAppendAdditionalGroups) find those functions, getSupplementalGroupsFromPath, the openUserFile string and moby/sys/user.ParseGroupFilter. The control programs were built with Go 1.27.1, CGO_ENABLED=0, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The vulnerable code is not in the shipped binary.
